issues.failure_explanation: The local projection error is not of order h^{k+1} in its H^{k+1} norm, so the displayed H^{k+1}-norm estimate cannot yield the next h^{k+1/2} bound. A valid trace estimate must separately use the L2 and H1 projection errors; that argument is absent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid step by an elementwise trace inequality involving h^{-1} times the L2 error and h times the H1 error, together with the corresponding projection approximation estimates under the curved-element mapping.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed DG approximation estimate, and hence the approximation contribution used in the main theorem, is not proved by the displayed calculation.
issues.title: Invalid trace approximation step in the DG projection estimate
issues.why_classification: This is a local standard projection-and-trace repair that preserves the claimed order and requires no change to the method or theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The DG norm controls volume values, boundary traces, and jumps, but not the individual interior-face trace $(\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I)^-$ occurring in L4. Cauchy–Schwarz therefore does not give the asserted mesh-independent continuity bound. Projection residuals can have a common nonzero trace across an interior face even when their jump is small, so the missing control cannot be recovered from the stated DG norm alone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a contained continuity estimate in a stronger trace/graph norm, or estimate L4 directly using trace approximation properties of the particular projection residual and then revise the theorem proof accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 is unsupported, and the step in the main theorem that absorbs the approximation bilinear form into the DG approximation error is consequently unreliable.
issues.title: The DG norm does not control the interior trace used in the continuity lemma
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a nontrivial additional trace estimate or a reformulated continuity lemma, although it may preserve the advertised convergence order.

issues.failure_explanation: A small displacement controls $u-u\circ\Phi_h^{-1}$ through derivatives of $u$, not through $\|u\|_{L^2}$ alone. The asserted inequality fails for rapidly varying functions: translation differences may be large relative to displacement times the L2 norm. Consequently, the first term in the lemma's stated bound requires at least H1-type regularity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a standard composition estimate with $h^{k+1}\|\tilde I\|_{H^1}$, followed by the trace inequality. The main theorem already assumes enough regularity to absorb the resulting H1 and H2 norms into its H^{k+1} term.
issues.overall_effect: The transformed-solution estimate and the bound for the common inflow-boundary term T1 in the main theorem are not established as written.
issues.title: Composition displacement is incorrectly bounded by the L2 norm of the function
issues.why_classification: A standard local replacement preserves the rate and the main theorem's existing regularity regime, although the lemma's displayed norm must be corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item[$(A_2)$] 0 is the regular value of the function $f(x) = \Omega\cdot \boldsymbol{n}_h(x)$, that is, $\forall x\in f^{-1}(0)$, $\nabla f(x)\neq 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption A2 gives nonvanishing gradients separately for each h, but no h-uniform lower bound on $|\nabla f|$; hence the tubular constants need not be independent of h. Shape regularity and quasi-uniformity also do not by themselves bound the total length of all facewise zero sets. These two unproved uniform assertions are exactly what the global $O(h^k)$ estimate requires.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and verify uniform transversality and uniform geometric-complexity assumptions for the characteristic set, or supply a new global geometric argument deriving those properties from stronger mesh-to-boundary approximation hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted measure estimate for the mismatch between the mapped and computational inflow boundaries is not justified under the stated assumptions.
issues.title: Regular-value and mesh assumptions do not give a uniform tubular-area bound
issues.why_classification: A complete repair needs substantive uniform geometric hypotheses or a new geometric lemma, but it can retain a comparable boundary-mismatch estimate for uniformly transverse mesh families.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the term $T_3$, let $D_c$ denote the set of boundary elements intersected by the characteristic boundary $\Gamma^0_h$, which means $D_c =\{K\in \mathcal{T}_h:\partial K\cap \Gamma^0\neq \emptyset\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (3.8) is a function-error estimate and says nothing about $Vol(D_c)$. For a regular characteristic set, the union of boundary elements meeting it typically has volume of order h^2 in both dimensions considered: in 3D it surrounds an O(1)-length curve with cross-sectional scale h^2, and in 2D it contains finitely many elements of area h^2. This is not $O(h^{k+1})$ for k≥2. Substituting the natural $O(h^2)$ scaling into the paper's own trace calculation yields only an $O(h^k)$ bound for T3, not $O(h^{k+1/2})$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must derive a sharper estimate for T3 without the false volume bound, or weaken the theorem's rate to the order supported by the corrected calculation.
issues.overall_effect: The central optimal DG convergence rate is not proved; the displayed argument loses at least one half-order in the geometric inflow-boundary term.
issues.title: False volume scaling of characteristic boundary elements drives the optimal-rate proof
issues.why_classification: The source supplies no valid route to recover the advertised optimal half-order. Its available calculation supports only a materially weaker rate, so preserving the main guarantee would require new proof architecture.
